how: Hong Kong studios run perfume-blending workshops where participants compose a custom fragrance in about 90 minutes.
Tufting studios such as Tufting Dept run short workshops where beginners tuft a small rug or coaster with a tufting gun.
Urban Sketchers Hong Kong and related groups (Drawn Here, Sketch Hong Kong) hold on-location sketching sessions and introductory workshops.
venue: Urban Sketchers Hong Kong / HKU SPACE

how: The Hong Kong Arts Centre offers multi-week evening courses in botanical watercolour and drawing for adults.
venue: Hong Kong Arts Centre / Hong Kong Art School

how: Hong Kong Art School and Hong Kong Arts Centre run ceramics and clay workshops, including pottery-throwing courses.
MakerBay is a large Tsuen Wan makerspace with digital fabrication tools and public classes.
MakerBay and other maker-education groups run Arduino and Raspberry Pi robotics classes open to the public.
Cosplay centres on large annual conventions such as Ani-Com & Games and Hong Kong Comic Con at the convention centre.
A Games Workshop store in Mong Kok stocks Warhammer ranges and has held painting and modelling workshops.

activity: Artisan bread and pastry baking courses
how: Cooking studios such as Foodcraft in Kennedy Town and restaurant Roganic run bread and baking classes.
Conspiracy Chocolate in Wong Chuk Hang has run bean-to-bar workshops covering stone-grinding, tempering and moulding.
Lantau Mama, Loula Natural and Roganic offer classes on kombucha, kefir and other ferments.
MONO runs small-group sourdough masterclasses, and Foodcraft offers a Level 1 sourdough class.
Sino Centre in Mong Kok gathers shops selling comics, anime goods and collectible toys.
Record shops in Sham Shui Po, Yau Ma Tei and Central sell second-hand vinyl across cantopop, jazz and classical.
venue: Kubrick (Yau Ma Tei) and Sham Shui Po record shops

how: Boat eco-tours from Tung Chung and Tai O watch wild Chinese white dolphins in north Lantau waters (dolphins, not whales).
Coffee Break Language Exchange holds weekly meetups where people practise languages in small groups.
Hong Kong Philosophy Cafe runs English-language discussion evenings at the Fringe Club.
venue: Hong Kong Philosophy Cafe at Fringe Club

how: A Plastic Ocean Foundation and Beyond Plastic organise regular volunteer clean-ups of non-gazetted beaches with gloves and pickers provided.
CITY RUNNERS (RunOurCity Foundation) runs about 30 neighbourhood running groups with free beginner trial sessions.
Asia Society Hong Kong Center has run beginner-friendly tai chi sessions, and free morning tai chi has been held at Hong Kong Park.
Hong Kong Rock Climbing Adventure leads guided canyoning trips down Ping Nam stream with waterfall abseils.
Wakeboarding is available behind boats at Tai Tam and Tai Po, but no cable park was found.
Hong Kong has sport-climbing crags and sea cliffs but no big walls; the nearest multi-pitch big-wall climbing is in mainland China, e.g. Yangshuo in Guangxi.
BASE jumping is not offered in Hong Kong because of dense urban airspace and the lack of legal jump sites; it is practised in mainland China and elsewhere.
No skydiving drop zone operates in Hong Kong because of its congested, restricted airspace; tandem jumps are available in mainland China and Southeast Asia.
Hong Kong has no flooded cave systems for cave diving; the nearest are in mainland China and elsewhere in Asia.
Hong Kong has no significant cave systems for caving; the nearest are in Guangxi and Guizhou, mainland China.
Hong Kong has no luge track or mountain luge facility because it lacks the terrain; the sport is practised in Europe, North America and East Asia.
Hong Kong has no rivers large enough for white water rafting; the nearest rafting is on rivers in Guangdong, mainland China.
